title: [DAP] Debug attempts in Helix time out when nonstandard events are received
body:
### Summary

Hey! I really like Helix, and I've been trying to get debugging Python with it to work, to be able to ditch PyCharm.

I'm aware of the experimental status of DAP support - this is a more general question on how Helix should handle events unique to the DAP provider, since that seems to be the reason for my (current) problems.

### Reproduction Steps

<!-- Ideally provide a key sequence and/or asciinema.org recording. --> 

All of the below is to happen in a virtual environment with debugpy installed, e.g. via `pip install -U debugpy`.

Take the following file (e.g. as `debug.py`):

```python

def fn(a: int) -> int:
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    else:
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    b = 2
    # I wanted to place the breakpoint on the following line, and inspect the stack.
    c = fn(b)
```

I am using the following debugger template for it, which I found in one of the Python DAP-related issues:

```toml
[[language]]
name = "python"

[language.debugger]
name = "debugpy"
transport = "stdio"
command = "python3"
args = ["-m",  "debugpy.adapter"]

[[language.debugger.templates]]
name = "source"
request = "launch"
completion = [ { name = "entrypoint", completion = "filename", default = "." } ]
args = { mode = "debug", program = "{0}"}
```

1. `hx debug.py`
2. `<space>G`, then `l`, then select the `source` template, then select `debug.py` as file (possibly via tab completion).

Subsequently, the debugger process (?) times out. As can be deduced from the attached log, it seems that Helix's DAP transport cannot deal with the `debugpySockets` event, which was added in recent versions of `debugpy`. This to me raises the question how Helix can be made to deal with these non-standard events in a more general way, since other DAP implementations might also roll their own custom events.

When downgrading to an earlier version of debugpy that does not send the `debugpySockets` event (I tried v1.8.0), starting debugging puts the editor in the background in a suspended state, and results in weird output on the terminal, which is another issue in and of itself.

PS: I am happy to work on this, I just do not have a lot of experience in Rust, so it might take a while.

### Helix log

<details><summary>~/.cache/helix/helix.log</summary>

```
2024-09-25T15:40:33.914 helix_dap::transport [ERROR] err: <- Parse(Error("unknown variant `debugpySockets`, expected one of `initialized`, `stopped`, `continued`, `exited`, `terminated`, `thread`, `output`, `breakpoint`, `module`, `loadedSource`, `process`, `capabilities`, `memory`", line: 0, column: 0))
```

</details>


### Platform

macOS

### Terminal Emulator

iTerm2

### Installation Method

Homebrew

### Helix Version

helix 24.7 (079f5442)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi Nicholas! Much like you, I like Helix and am trying to get DAP up and running without much experience. I have the impression that the message with the unexpected `event` value triggered a [break in a communication loop](https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/blob/81708b70e685426716999e1278b7373292e797e9/helix-dap/src/transport.rs#L285), causing DAP to shut down.

According to the [DAP specification](https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/specification#Base_Protocol_Event), there are a few predefined event types, but the event type itself is a string. Helix's deserialization logic assumes no undocumented event type values are used, which seems to cause the above behavior.

I assume it's safe to let Helix ignore the `debugpySockets` event in the [grand scheme of things](https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/overview). To do this, the deserialization logic would need to be modified. Many Rust applications including Helix use the `serde` library for this to do most of the heavy lifting behind the scenes.

I can still resume Helix using the `fg` shell command at that point. Looking more closely at the essence of the error, it looks like debug is in the wrong working directory: ``` ImportError: can't find '__main__' module in '/var/home//Desktop/helix/target/debug' ``` I started the debugger while `~/Desktop/main.py` was open, without entering an entrypoint.
